title: Berlin Snow Clearing Rules - Quick Summary
items: **BSR clears the road, you clear the pavement.** Berlin's street cleaning law gives BSR the carriageway, the cycle paths, the crossings and the bus stops. The pavement in front of a building belongs to the **Anlieger**, which is the owner, or a tenant if the lease says so.

**How wide depends on your street's cleaning class.** It is **1.5 metres** on main roads and shopping streets, the register's categories **A1 and A2**, and **1 metre** everywhere else. Across Berlin's roughly **11,400 kilometres** of registered street sides, **19 percent** carry the wider duty and **81 percent** the metre.

**The clock is 07:00, or 09:00 on a Sunday.** Snow goes as soon as the snowfall stops. If it is still falling after **20:00** or starts later, the path has to be clear by **07:00** the next morning, and by **09:00** on a Sunday or public holiday. The route to your bins needs to be one bin wide by **06:00**.

**Grit, never salt.** Every de-icing agent is banned for residents in Berlin, not just salt. Use **sand, grit or granulate**. In a hard frost, gritting alone is not enough: break the ice up, lift it off, then grit.

**Nearly a quarter of Berlin streets change class partway along.** **2,564** of **11,377** street entries in the register carry more than one class, so your neighbour three doors down can owe a different width from you.

**On category C streets the road is yours too.** That is **1,684 kilometres**, about 15 percent of the city, and it is concentrated outside the ring: **32 percent** of Marzahn-Hellersdorf's street sides and **27 percent** of Treptow-Köpenick's, against effectively none in Mitte or Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg.
**The fine reaches 10,000 euros.** Hiring a firm or a neighbour is allowed, but the responsibility and the duty to check stay with you, and an injured pedestrian can claim on top of the fine.
